title: Interval-Calibrated Noisy Quantization: A Parameter-Free Defense Against Quantization-Gap Attacks

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to defend against quantization-gap attacks without requiring impractical per-model grid searches to set noise scales. Paper [1] studies quantization's adverse effects from a security perspective but does not propose defenses against quantization-gap attacks. Paper [12] investigates fault injection attacks on quantized models but does not address quantization-gap attacks or defenses. Paper [18] introduces a backdoor attack exploiting quantization but does not address defenses against quantization-gap attacks. No prior paper explicitly addresses the same problem of defending against quantization-gap attacks while avoiding grid searches.

### Mechanism
The contribution's mechanism derives Gaussian noise scale directly from quantization interval half-widths, computing sigma-hat as the median of per-layer half-widths with a single pass over weights and no evaluation data. Paper [30] uses the median absolute deviation (MAD) for noise estimation in adaptive ISTA, which is conceptually equivalent to the use of MAD for estimating sigma-hat in this contribution. While the application differs, the underlying primitive of using MAD for noise estimation is equivalent. Paper [15] also uses MAD for noise estimation in image processing, further supporting mechanism coverage.

### Evaluation
The evaluation demonstrates that the computed sigma-hat falls within 22% of the grid-search optimal sigma*. Paper [7] describes an algorithm for optimizing quantization scales by an arbitrary quality measure, which involves grid-search-like optimization but does not use the same evaluation design as this contribution. Paper [10] benchmarks robustness of quantized models but does not use the same evaluation design. No prior paper uses the specific evaluation design of comparing sigma-hat to grid-search optimal sigma* for quantization-gap defense. Thus, the evaluation design is novel.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of post-training LLM quantization security. Paper [1] explicitly addresses security risks in LLM quantization, and Paper [12] investigates fault injection attacks on quantized LLMs. Both papers work in the same general application area of post-training LLM quantization security, even though they target different specific problems. Therefore, the domain is covered.
